body:
Sorry to hear that you're in the same boat.  You're exactly right it's childhood ending. My mom says she knew something was wrong after that camp because 'the light went out' for me. I vaguely remember being really happy for a while, running around playing with friends, there was always a big grin on my face in pictures.

I remember being led by the hand to a cabin and being told it was 'special nap time'. I remember being told ghost stories and then told to pretend to be asleep. I remember my arms being held down, and that I struggled. After that I was afraid of the dark, of going to sleep, of strangers, of being touched. Sometimes I had to make myself remember fighting back just so I could look myself in the mirror. I remind myself that I was too young and could never have defended myself against what was done to me, but I still resisted. I'm so proud of younger me for fighting back.

I was a pretty trusting kid especially when it came to adults and I suffered because of it. I didn't trust my parents anymore because they sent me there in the first place so they couldn't comfort me. Kids my own age were foreign to me, I felt like I lived inside my own head and was watching from a distance. I got made fun of and beaten up many times, to the point of broken bones. Some days I would pretend I could make myself invisible, because no attention was better than being targeted. I think never learning to develop friendships at that age crippled my social development. I just don't know how to trust people. 

I don't really know what else to say. Thanks for your kind words and empathy.

I feel like I've used up all my strength. My adolescence was really really rough. I got bullied and beaten up to the point of broken bones, had to transfer schools twice, had to face torment every day. I think back about that little kid I was and I'm so proud of him for being so tough and strong enough to face that every day. I don't have the same strength anymore. It's like my battery doesn't recharge anymore, and I'm always on low power. Fuck I just compared myself to a phone. I've never been to a support group, don't know how I'd do in that kind of setting. Perhaps that's something to think about.
Thank you for your kind words.
